title: Longest Arithmetic Subsequence
summary: Given an array of integers, find the length of the longest subsequence where the difference between consecutive elements is the same.
statement: Given an array of integers, find the length of the longest subsequence where the difference between consecutive elements is the same. A subsequence is derived from the original array by removing some or no elements while maintaining the order of the remaining elements. An arithmetic sequence is defined as a sequence where the difference between consecutive elements is constant.
constraints: At least two integers are provided.
Return the longest order-preserving subsequence with constant adjacent difference.
hints: A subsequence ending at j is identified by its final difference.
Store the best length for every (ending index,difference).
Extend dp[i][difference], defaulting a new pair to length two.
Every arithmetic subsequence has a unique prior endpoint and difference captured by this transition.
editorial: Every arithmetic subsequence has a unique prior endpoint and difference captured by this transition.

tests.explanation: All four values form an arithmetic sequence with difference three.
Four, seven, and ten form length three.
